issue_context.title: The type initializer sometimes doesn't execute for an empty struct
comments: Seems like this is only reproducible with PublishAot.

> first invocation of any instance or virtual method of that type if it is a value type

Is it applicable to boxed `ToString`? The method is provided by base type `ValueType`.

> Seems like this is only reproducible with PublishAot.

It does reproduce without PublishAot.

> It does reproduce without PublishAot.

I tested with .NET 8 and .NET 9 daily build, can't reproduce without PublishAot=true.

Tested on .NET 8:

```
> dotnet --version
8.0.202
> dotnet run -c Release
Foo`1[Bar]
0
```

Which platform is it? This is linux-x64 with 8.0.202 and 9.0.100-preview.4.24180.1 https://github.com/am11/CrossRepoCITesting/actions/runs/8498315034/job/23277887637

```sh
$ dotnet run
Foo`1[Bar]
42

$ dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true -c Release -o out
$ out/gh-100466
Foo`1[Bar]
0
```
Same results on linux-arm64 and osx-arm64.

> Which platform is it? This is linux-x64 with 8.0.202 and 9.0.100-preview.4.24180.1 [am11/CrossRepoCITesting/actions/runs/8498315034/job/23277887637](https://github.com/am11/CrossRepoCITesting/actions/runs/8498315034/job/23277887637)
>

> $ dotnet run
> Foo`1[Bar]
> 42
> 
> $ dotnet publish -p:PublishAot=true -c Release -o out
> $ out/gh-100466
> Foo`1[Bar]
> 0
> ```
> 
> Same results on linux-arm64 and osx-arm64.

I'm on Windows 11 x64.
Yes, on win-x64 it returns 0 with JIT as well.

> Yes, on win-x64 it returns 0 with JIT as well.

I updated the issue to reflect output from different configurations and platforms.

This case is covered by `Thus for value types, the .cctor is only guaranteed to be called for instances of the value type that are not “all-zero”.` from the ECMA-335 spec.

For determinism, we always trigger the type initializers as late as possible. Thus, the expected behavior in this case is `0`.

review_comments: Are `ref struct` types unique enough to warrant an added case here?

The two cases in the PR provide full code coverage for the two interesting cases in the current implementation. The path taken by `ref struct`s wrt cctors is covered by the non-ref struct test cases.

It is hard to predict future interesting cases that may be introduced. If somebody changes the implementation to introduce more interesting cases in future, I hope that will do due diligence and add test coverage for it.

Nit: I realize this is annoying, but I think this sort of test should possibly be under `runtime/src/tests/Loader`. It can also be named something like `StaticTypeInitialization`, which would be clearer. I'm also fine with it not being renamed, but the location under `Loader` does seem more appropriate.

I do not think about this issue as a classloader bug.

This bug was in the implementation of boxing. Boxing implementation had a superfluous cctor trigger on one path that made it do more than what it was supposed to in some cases. Boxing is a JIT-centric concept - the basic tests are under https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/tree/main/src/tests/JIT/Methodical/Boxing.

The bug intersects with cctor triggers. Cctor triggers are JIT-centric concept too - the basic tests are under https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/tree/main/src/tests/JIT/Methodical/cctor.

The bug is not in the type initialization management, like the logic that caches exceptions thrown by cctors or that breaks cycles between cctors. Type initialization management would be classloader - the basic tests are under https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/tree/main/src/tests/Loader/classloader/TypeInitialization.

The intersection of JIT/Methodical/Boxing and JIT/Methodical/cctor gives JIT/Regressions.

This is my though process for the current location, but I do not have a strong opinion about it. I am happy to move it if you tell me where you would like to see it moved to exactly.
